mechanism_narrative: An increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPI) above 2% year-over-year signals inflationary pressure, leading to tighter monetary policy expectations and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or CPI YoY growth > 2% does not correlate with subsequent tightening actions by the Fed.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 4% signals a tight labor market, which historically leads to wage inflation and increased corporate costs, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or UNRATE < 4% does not correlate with subsequent wage inflation.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month increase in housing starts (HOUST) signals strengthening consumer demand, which boosts corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns in expansionary demand periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 2% month-over-month signals a contraction in economic activity, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or INDPRO MoM decline > 2% does not correlate with subsequent economic contraction.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 3% and the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) shows year-over-year growth below 1%, the real interest rate is high, signaling a restrictive monetary policy that leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the combination of high FEDFUNDS and low CPIAUCSL growth does not correlate with subsequent negative returns.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) by more than 300,000 in a month signals strong labor market conditions, which boosts consumer spending and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or PAYEMS increase > 300,000 does not correlate with subsequent consumer spending growth.

mechanism_narrative: When real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) grow by more than 5% year-over-year and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) is below 5%, it signals robust consumer demand and low unemployment, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
regime_hint: robust consumer demand and low unemployment
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the combination of high RSAFS growth and low UNRATE does not correlate with subsequent positive returns.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month decline in real GDP (GDPC1) signals an economic slowdown, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 60-day forward returns in slowdown periods are not significantly lower than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).
